Thanks for the demo last week — product looks promising. Before we move to an expanded pilot, procurement and engineering asked me to clarify how Redwood structures the SLA and premium support packaging when customers require higher uptime bands and faster escalation windows. A few specific asks: 

- Does uptime crediting materially change if we opt into automated regional failover vs. active-active?
- How do response time tiers map to escalation coverage (hours / roster / on-call)? Is there a clear incremental price for 15m vs 60m response SLAs?
- For customers committing to N committed GAUs (usage) or an annual spend threshold, what bulk/volume discounting do you typically apply to premium response packs? Are there look-up slabs or is it negotiated per-deal?
- Any constraints around credits calculation during partial outages (regional vs global)?

Procurement copied this thread; attaching our high-level requirements file. We’re trying to size the cost delta for 99.95% -> 99.99% and an add-on for 24/7 escalation coverage.

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the requirements. Putting short answers up-front, then a suggested next step (call + MAP):

1) Uptime credits and failover model
- Active-active with cross-region replication: credits are measured on per-region degraded capacity and do not automatically nullify credits for other regions; typical crediting follows the % of affected GAU-hours.
- Automated regional failover (single-active, auto-failover): we treat failover as a resilience feature and the crediting is slightly more conservative (we assume failover mitigates some impact) — you still get credits for sustained degraded throughput post-failover.

2) Response tiers -> escalation coverage
- 60m SLA (priority lane): standard business-hours triage + oncall rotation during OOS incidents (included in Tier 1).
- 15m SLA (critical lane): 24/7 on-call rota with senior escalation (Tier 2).
- The incremental price between 60m and 15m is largely driven by on-call staffing and retainer sizing; typical incremental uplift is 22—35% on the premium support add-on depending on scale and region.

3) Volume / bulk discounts
- We publish commit bands (small/medium/large) that give step-down pricing for premium packs at 3 commit levels (>= $250k/year, >= $750k/year, >= $2.5M/year).
- For larger or strategic pilots we move to bespoke slabs or multi-year commit credits.

4) Partial outages
- Credits pro-rate by affected region and service surface (inference vs control plane). We’ll include concrete examples in the one-pager.

Next step: Ben (cc’d) can stitch a one-pager with simple examples (99.95% -> 99.99% credit math, two scenarios for failover) and a draft MAP with milestone-based discounts. Can we do a 30-min call Thursday 10:30am PT? I’ll attach a sketch now.

Thanks Priya — quick answers below and a proposed MAP item list (short bullets). Replying inline to your clarifying points.

> For the failover treatment: if we choose active-active for inference but keep control-plane single-region (for latency), how do you blend the crediting? Is it hybrid?

- Short answer: hybrid. Inference availability credits will be measured per-inference-region; control-plane outages are calculated separately. If the control plane outage causes inference disruption we treat it as correlated and credit according to the primary impact window. We’ll provide two worked examples in the MAP doc.

> Do the commit bands you mentioned apply to the premium response packs only, or to uptime/add-on credits?

- Commit bands reduce the price of premium response packs (the human/time component) and we also apply a modest discount to retainer-priced uptime credits when bundled. Pure ad-hoc credits for past incidents are not discounted.

> Does prepaying for Tier 2 retainer yield bigger discount than buying credits ad-hoc?

- Yes. Prepaying retainer + multi-year commit typically yields the largest effective discount because it locks capacity on our on-call roster and reduces staffing variance. That’s where you see the 15—25% extra improvement vs. ad-hoc ticket credits.

- Ben to deliver a 1-page pricing matrix + 2 worked examples (99.95% -> 99.99%; regional failover case) — ETA: EOD Wednesday (attached).
- Markus to prepare a preliminary quote with commit-band pricing — ETA: Friday COB.
- Priya / Procurement to share 12-month forecast banding (CSV) before Friday so we can run a tailored slab.
